rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request is included in the account of blessings: God grants what they asked for by ordering them down to a town, although their ingratitude deserved wrath.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنه داخل في تعداد النعم وتفصيلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their declaration that they could not endure one food signals aversion to the manna and quails and failure to thank God for an effortless provision.
rows.anchor: فإنه يدل على كراهيتم إياه إذ الصبر حبس النفس في المضيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode resembles their earlier resistance after hearing God's speech, followed by their destruction and then the gift of life.
rows.anchor: حيث عاندوا بعد سماع الكلام وأهلكوا ثم أفاض عليهم نعمة الحياة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi argues that the request could not be sinful because God answered it, since answering a sinful request would itself be sinful and prophets cannot do that.
rows.anchor: ما قال الإمام الرازي لو كان سؤالهم معصية لما أجابهم لأن الإجابة إلى المعصية معصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author endorses al-Salikuti's judgment that al-Razi's inference is weak: granting the request does not make their ungrateful demand virtuous.
rows.anchor: قال مولانا الساليكوتي ومن هذا ظهر ضعف ما قال الإمام الرازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One food can mean a single, unchanging regimen, even if it consists of the two foods manna and quails.
rows.anchor: بإعتبار كونه على نهج واحد كما يقال :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the Israelites sought familiar agricultural produce because manna and quails were luxurious foods unlike their usual fare.
rows.anchor: من طعام أهل التلذذ والسرف وكأن القوم كانوا فلاحة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported explanation says they cooked manna and quails together, making one dish.
rows.anchor: إنهم كانوا يطبخونهما معا فيصير طعاما واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls it a weak account that the request preceded the descent of the quails.
rows.anchor: والقول بأن هذا القول كان قبل نزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is even less plausible that “one food” meant only quails because manna was a drink or sweetener and therefore supposedly did not count as another food.
rows.anchor: وأهون منه القول بأنهم أرادوا بالطعام الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal that a singular “one” stands for two foods is still less plausible; the cited comparison uses a dual expression for pearls that come from only one sea.
rows.anchor: وإلا نزل القول بأنه عبر بالواحد عن الإثنين كما عبر بالإثنين عن الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase asks Moses to pray on their behalf for the listed produce; the conjunction marks their impatience as the reason for asking.
rows.anchor: فأدع لنا ربك أي سله لأجلنا بدعائك إياه بأن يخرج لنا كذا وكذا

rows.speaker: بنو عامر
rows.claim: Banu ʿAmir read the imperative with kasra on its final letter, treating دعا like the defective verb رمى.
rows.anchor: ولغة بني عامر ( فأدع ) بكسر العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They asked Moses to pray because prophetic prayers are more likely to be answered; more generally, one person's prayer for another is especially apt to be answered.
rows.anchor: لأن دعاء الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام أقرب للإجابة من دعاء غيرهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet asked ʿUmar to include him among those for whom he prayed.
rows.anchor: لهذا قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لعمر رضي الله تعالى عنه : أشركنا

rows.speaker: الأثر
rows.claim: A transmitted saying urges prayer through tongues that have not disobeyed God, understood here as other people's tongues.
rows.anchor: وفي الأثر أدعوني بألسنة لم تعصوني فيها وحملت على ألسنة الغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God “Lord” prepares the grounds for the prayer's acceptance.
rows.anchor: والتعرض لعنوان الربوبية لتمهيد مبادي الإجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say “your Lord” because Moses had a special intimacy with God through His favor, direct speech, and the Torah, as if asking him to pray to the benefactor who favored him.
rows.anchor: لأن في ذلك من الإختصاص به ما ليس فيهم من مناجاته وتكليمه وإيتائه التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “bring forth” is a figurative consequence of literal extraction: it means producing by creation, not merely revealing what was hidden.
rows.anchor: المراد بالإخراج المعنى المجازي اللازم للمعنى الحقيقي وهو الإظهار بطريق الإيجاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The literal reading would require the earth to be an extractor and make the statement nonsensical.
rows.anchor: وما يصلح له ههنا هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb يخرج is jussive as the response to the imperative; Basran grammarians do not allow explaining its jussive with an omitted لام الطلب.
rows.anchor: مجزوم لأنه جواب الأمر وجزمه بلام الطلب محذوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first من is partitive: they ask for some of what the earth grows, specifically some edible produce.
rows.anchor: الأولى تبعيضية أي مأكولا بعض ما

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash treats the first من as extra, a parsing the author rejects.
rows.anchor: وأدعى الأخفش زيادتها وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is a relative pronoun with its object omitted; Abu al-Baqa rejects taking it as a verbal noun because the implied referent would be a substance.
rows.anchor: والعائد محذوف أي تنبته وجعلها مصدرية لم يجوزه أبو البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing growth to the earth is figurative, treating the receptacle as the agent; God placed the receptive capacity in the clay layer of the earth.
rows.anchor: مجاز من باب النسبة إلى القاب وقد أودع الله تعالى في الطبقة الطينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Locating the receptive power in the seed rather than the soil could lead to the claim that seeds have existed eternally as a kind.
rows.anchor: وكون القوة القابلة مودعة في الحب دون التراب ربما يفضي إلى القول بقدم الحب بالنوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second من may be explanatory, with the phrase functioning as a circumstantial expression meaning “being among the greens.”
rows.anchor: فالظرف مستقر واقع موقع الحال اي كائنا من

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan instead takes the second من as partitive, in apposition to ما, with the phrase attached directly to يخرج.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : تبعيضية واقعة موقع البدل

rows.speaker: الساليكوتي
rows.claim: Al-Salikuti says both parsings imply that they sought only some of the listed items; treating the second من as explanatory alongside the first partitive would lose that meaning and suggest all items.
rows.anchor: كما قال الساليكوتي يفيد أن المطلوب إخراج بعض هؤلاء

rows.speaker: المولى عصام الدين
rows.claim: Mawla ʿIsam al-Din's explanatory parsing would leave the wording implying that all listed plants were requested, since there is no prior specification.
rows.anchor: المولى عصام الدينل خلا الكلام عن الإفادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baql is a generic term for fresh plants eaten by people or animals; here it means edible herbs and greens.
rows.anchor: والبقل جنس يندرج فيه النبات الرطب مما يأكله الناس والأنعام والمراد به هنا أطابيب البقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The familiar qiththa is identified as cucumber; al-Khalil also says it means cucumber.
rows.anchor: والقثاء هو هذا المعروف وقال الخليل : هو الخيار

rows.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب وغيره
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab and others read قثاء with damma on qaf, a dialect form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يحيى إبن وثاب وغيرهبضم القاف وهو لغة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the language authorities agree that الفوم means wheat and other grains used for baking.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : لا خلاف عند أهل اللغة أنا لقوما

rows.speaker: الكسائي وجماعة
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi and a group identify الفوم as garlic; the text explains the reading through substitution of ثاء for فاء.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي وجماعة : هو الثوم وقد أدل

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud's reading as garlic fits its pairing with onion and lentils, and the author's teacher inclines to that reading.
rows.anchor: قرأ إبن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه ونفس شيخنا عليه الرحمة إليه تميل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas is quoted as identifying الفوم with bread; the author says this can be understood as a word also applied to bread, though bread is unlikely here because it grows neither from earth nor alongside greens.
rows.anchor: وما في المعالم عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما منا لقوما لخبز يمكن توجيهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One rationale for the sequence is its balance of hot, cold, moist, and dry qualities: greens encompass varieties, followed by cucumber, garlic, lentils, and onion.
rows.anchor: وجه ترتيب النظم أنه ذكر أولا ما هو جامع للحرارة والبرودة والرطوبة واليبوسة وهو البقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another rationale is that the list starts with food eaten without fire, then gives foods that should be cooked; onion may become cold and moist after cooking according to some.
rows.anchor: ذكر أولا ما يؤكل من غير علاج نار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question أتستبدلون is a fresh sentence answering the implied question of what Moses or God said.
rows.anchor: إستئناف وقع جوابا عن سؤال مقدر كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker may be God speaking through Moses, which suits the surrounding enumeration of blessings, or Moses himself, which better fits the discourse sequence.
rows.anchor: والقائل إما الله تعالى على لسان موسى عليه السلام ويرجحه كون المقام مقام تعداد النعم أو موسى نفسه وهو الأنسب بسياق النظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative rebukes them, and الاستبدال means exchanging one thing for another.
rows.anchor: والإستفهام للإنكار والإستبدال الإعتياض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although inability to endure one food might imply wanting an addition, their aversion and ingratitude imply a wish to remove the blessing and replace it.
rows.anchor: يدل على كراهتم ذلك الطعام وعدم الشكر على النعمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported view says they explicitly sought replacement, and the reply signals that receiving the requested food would mean losing manna and quails rather than combining the foods.
rows.anchor: إنهم طلبوا ذلك وخطابهم بهذا إشارة إلى أنه تعالى إذا أعطاهم ما سألوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation that the exchange takes place in the stomach is dismissed.
rows.anchor: الإستبدال في المعدة وهو كما ترى

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy read أتبدلون; this is figurative because God effects the change, but their request causes it, so they are described as exchangers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي أتبدلون وهو مجاز لأن التبديل ليس لهم إنما ذلك إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object is the thing they would obtain, while the noun with باء denotes what would be relinquished; أدنى qualifies the latter.
rows.anchor: دخلت عليه الباء هو الزائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أدنى may derive from nearness or be inverted from دون, meaning inferior; on the first derivation, nearness is metaphorically used for low worth, as distance is used for honor.
rows.anchor: إما من الدنو أو مقلوب من الدون وهو على الثاني ظاهر

rows.speaker: زهير والكسائي
rows.claim: Zuhayr and al-Kisaʾi read أدنا with hamza, supporting derivation from الدناءة with hamza changed into alif.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة زهير والكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The better food is manna and quails; its superiority lies in greater value, taste, benefit, ease of acquisition, and freedom from doubt about its lawfulness.
rows.anchor: ومعنى خيرية هذا المأكول بالنسبة إلى ذلك غلاء قيمته وطيب لذته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أهبطوا مصرا is a separate reported sentence; it is unjoined because the first is declarative and the second is not, and because descending explains how they could exchange foods.
rows.anchor: جملة محكية بالقول كالأولى وإنما لم يعطف إحداهما على الأخرى في المحكى لأن الأولى خبر معنى وهذه ليست كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If both sentences are spoken by the same speaker, their separation has the stated grammatical rationale; if Moses and God speak them separately, the lack of conjunction is self-explanatory.
rows.anchor: هذا إذا جعل الجملتان من كلام الله تعالى أو كلام موسى وإن جعل إحداهما من موسى والأخرى من الله تعالى فوجه الفصل ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pause after خبر is sufficient under the same-speaker analysis and complete under the two-speaker analysis.
rows.anchor: والوقف على خبر كاف على الأول وتام على الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Descent may be spatial, if the wilderness is higher than the town, or a descent in rank; the contextual sense is the latter.
rows.anchor: وأن يكون رتبيا وهو الأنسب بالمقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has أهبطوا with damma on both hamza and ba.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( أهبطوا ) بضم الهمزة والباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مصر means a great town and originally denotes a boundary between two things; a quoted poetic line uses it for the boundary dividing day and night.
rows.anchor: وأصله الحد والحاجز بين الشيئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deriving the town name from milking every drop from a sheep is far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وأخذه من مصرت الشاة أمصرها إذا حلبت كل شيء في ضرعها بعيد

rows.speaker: أشهب عن مالك
rows.claim: Ashhab relates that Malik identified the place as Egypt, his town, where Pharaoh lived, making مصر a proper name.
rows.anchor: وحكى عن أشهب أنه قال : قال لي مالك : هي مصر قريتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Place names can be masculine when considered as places and feminine when considered as lands; if مصر is a feminine town name it takes tanwin because its middle consonant is still.
rows.anchor: وأسماء المواضع قد تعتبر من حيث المكانية فتذكر وقد تعتبر من حيث الأرضية فتؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that مصر is a proper name is supported by Ibn Masʿud's codex spelling it without alif after ra, but opposed by the Qur'anic tanwin and by the command to enter the holy land, understood as Syria, which implies they were confined to the wilderness.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد ما قاله الإمام مالك رضي الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some derive مصر from the Arabicized Misraim, a son of Noah who first laid out the city; Arabicization permits declension because foreignness no longer governs the form.
rows.anchor: ومن اناس من جعل ( مصر ) معرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You will have what you asked” explains the order to descend; al-Bahr instead calls it an answer to the imperative, which can be answered by a clause, with an implied link and pronoun: “therein” and “what you asked for.”
rows.anchor: فإن لكم ما سألتم تعليل للأمر بالهبوط وفي البحر أنها جواب للأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the requested items simply ما avoids naming them directly as a sign of disdain.
rows.anchor: والتعبير عن الأشياء المسئولة ب ( ما )

rows.speaker: النخعي ويحيى
rows.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi and Yahya read سألتم with kasra on the first letter.
rows.anchor: وقرأ النخعي ويحيى ( سألتم ) بكسر السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of humiliation being laid over them evokes either a tent or dome set over people or clay plastered onto a wall; the metaphor conveys encompassing, adherence, and humiliation.
rows.anchor: أي جعل ذلك محيطا بهم إحاطة القبة بمن ضربت عليه أو ألصق بهم من ضرب الطين على الحائط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image alludes to their poll tax paid in submission, distinctive clothing that identifies them as Jews, ingrained miserliness and inner poverty, and their habit of displaying hardship to avoid increased tax.
rows.anchor: وذلك بما ضرب عليهم من الجزية التي يؤدونها عن يد وهم صاغرون وبما ألزموه من إظهار الزي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their humiliation is retribution for ingratitude toward the blessing, linking this punishment to the preceding account; the third-person pronoun includes all Jews through later generations and is not an instance of iltifat.
rows.anchor: وهذا الضرب مجازاة لهم على كفران تلك النعمة وبهذا أرتبطت الآية بما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: باءوا may mean they settled into worldly trials, afterlife punishment, or hardships in both worlds; it may also mean that wrath came upon them, so no object of “return” is needed.
rows.anchor: أي نزلوا وتمكنوا بما حل بهم من البلاء والنقم في الدنيا أو بما تحقق لهم من العذاب في العقبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations say they became fitting for wrath or deserved punishment; the author calls the latter account far-fetched.
rows.anchor: أو صاروا أحقاء به أو استحقوا العذاب بسببه وهو بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root باء first denotes equality of parts and then any equivalence or matching, as in saying someone is another's equal and in cited idioms and a prophetic warning.
rows.anchor: واصل البواء بالفتح والضم مساواة الأجزاء ثم أستعمل في كل مساواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing the wrath as coming from God heightens and magnifies its severity.
rows.anchor: وفي وصف الغضب بكونه من الله تعالى تعظيم لشأنه بعد تعظيم وتفخيم بعد تفخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers to the preceding humiliation, poverty, and wrath; its distance may reflect the intervening material, their surprising punishment despite being People of the Book, or the enormity of these deeds.
rows.anchor: أشار بذلك إلى ما سبق من ضرب الذلة والمسكنة والبوء بالغضب العظيم وإنما بعده لبعد بعضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal باء introduces an interpreted verbal noun; the nominal wording highlights repeated disbelief and killing over time or vividly recalls their ugly acts.
rows.anchor: والباء للسببية وهي داخلة على المصدر المؤل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs may mean miracles generally, Moses's nine signs, those nine and other miracles, revealed scriptural signs generally, the Torah or some of its verses, verses describing Muhammad, the stoning passages, or the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: إما المعجزات مطلقا أو التسع التي أتى بها موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing the signs to God intensifies the condemnation; disbelief is mentioned first because it is the gravest offense, then prophet-killing as its consequence or source.
rows.anchor: وفي إضافة الآيات إلى أسمه تعالى زيادة تشنيع عليهم وبدا سبحانه بكفرهم بآياته لأنه أعظم كل عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite plural النبيين appears fewer than الأنبياء, while the two forms are equivalent when definite, so the report that they killed three hundred prophets in one morning does not contradict the wording.
rows.anchor: وأتى بالنبيين الظاهر في القلة دون الأنبياء الظاهر في الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of “without right” is that they knew the murders were unjust: worldly desire, caprice, and excess drove them; on this reading the definite article points to a known right.
rows.anchor: للإيذان بأن ذلك بغير الحق عندهم إذ لم يكن أحد معتقدا حقية قتل أحد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A more apparent reading takes الحق generically, meaning no right at all; the parallel wording in 3:112 supports this and means the killings were unjust even in their own view.
rows.anchor: الأظهر أنها للجنس والمراد بغير حق أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may simply expose the escalating ugliness of their conduct—killing a prophet, killing a group, and doing so without right—which best fits the ordinary sense of prohibition regardless of the killer's beliefs.
rows.anchor: إظهار معايب صنيعهم فإنه قتل النبي ثم جماعة منهم ثم كونه بغير الحق

rows.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
rows.claim: A later scholar says the qualifier is useful if غير means “for a cause other than the truth”: they killed prophets for falsehood and to defend it.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المتأخرين : هذا كله إذا كان الغير بمعنى النفي

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says they claimed prophets were liars and their miracles deceptions, and killed them for this reason and to suppress what they regarded as truth.
rows.anchor: ما قاله القفال : من إنهم كانوا يقولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That false accusation explains many cases, but Isaiah, John, and Zechariah were killed for other reasons: Isaiah rebuked factional violence after a king's death, John was killed over a woman, and Zechariah was sawn in two inside a tree while fleeing the king.
rows.anchor: ولعل ذلك غالب أحوالهم وإلا فشعياء ويحيى وزكريا عليهم السلام لم يقتلوا لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent syntax makes بغير الحق a contested modifier governed by both disbelief and killing; al-Bahr attaches it to the nearby killing alone.
rows.anchor: ثم الظاهر أن الجار والمجرور مما تنازع فيه الكفر والقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An atheist alleges a contradiction between Israelite prophet-killing and God's promise to help His messengers.
rows.anchor: تناقضا وأجيب بأن المقتولين من الأنبياء والموعود بنصرهم الرسل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reply distinguishes the prophets who were killed from the messengers promised help.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن المقتولين من الأنبياء والموعود بنصرهم الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinction fails because 2:87 also says that some messengers were killed.
rows.anchor: يدل على أن المقتول رسل أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas is reported to say that God decreed that seventy thousand people would be killed for each prophet and thirty-five thousand for each caliph; the author finds this answer unsound.
rows.anchor: كما روى عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن الله تعالى قدر أن يقتل بكل نبي سبعين ألفا

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: The preferred answer limits the promised messengers to those commanded to fight; their exposure to death is not incompatible with divine wisdom.
rows.anchor: فالأحسن أن المراد بالرسل المأمورون بالقتال كما أجاب به بعض المحققين

rows.speaker: علي والحسن
rows.claim: ʿAli and, in one report, al-Hasan read يقتلون with a doubled qaf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي رضي الله تعالى عنه : يقتلون بالتشديد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: In another reading, al-Hasan uses second-person تقتلون, creating a shift in address.
rows.anchor: وتقتلون بالتاء فيكون ذلك من الالتفات

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafiʿ reads النبيين with hamza, as he does النبي and النبوة.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع بهمز النبيين وكذا النبي والنبوة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man addressed the Prophet as نبيء الله with hamza; the Prophet replied that he was نبي الله without hamza.
rows.anchor: بما روى أن رجلا قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يانبي الله بالهمز فقال لست بنبيء الله

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd traces نبأت to leaving the earth; the objection may have been to the ambiguity of “expelled by God,” not to the reading itself, and a prophet's use is not automatically permitted for people.
rows.anchor: بأن أبا زيد حكى نبأت من الأرض إذا خرجت منها فمنع لوهم أن معناه ياطريد الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation confines the prohibition to early Islam, when Jewish subterfuge was prevalent, as with replacing راعنا by انظرنا.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن النهي كان خاصا في صدر الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural نبيين is challenged because a passive participle is not normally given the sound masculine plural; a reply says the word is active, or that its original sense has faded so the common meaning permits the plural.
rows.anchor: جمع النبي على نبيين وهو فعيل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final ذلك points back to disbelief and prophet-killing as causes of the earlier punishments; a singular demonstrative can gather several matters by treating them as one mentioned event.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى الكفر والقتل الواقعين سببا لما تقدم وجازت الإشارة بالمفرد إلى متعدد للتأويل بالمذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following phrase gives the cause behind their disbelief and killings: earlier disobedience and transgression lead one sin to another, with the first cause emphasized because it might seem unexpected.
rows.anchor: وما بعدها سبب للسبب والمعنى إن الذي حملهم على الكفر بآيات الله تعالى وقتلهم الأنبياء إنما هو تقدم عصيانهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported alternative takes the causal باء to mean “with,” and links the demonstrative to the earlier punishment; it omits a conjunction to show that each wrongdoing independently deserves punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الباء بمعنى مع وقيل : الإشارة بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that alternative as repetitious and as losing the earlier subtle causal relation; it also leaves the demonstrative without a clear purpose.
rows.anchor: وضعف هذا الوجه بأن التكرار خلاف الأصل مع فوات معنى لطيف حصل بالأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spiritual lesson is that they refused God's decree, gratitude, and patience; tyranny and abasement took hold, worldly love filled their hearts, and they fell from their high station.
rows.anchor: وحظ العارف من هذه الآيات الإعتبار بحال هؤلاء الذين لم يرضوا بالقضاء ولم يشكروا على النعماء ولم يصبروا على البلواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the mystical reading, the one food is wisdom and knowledge, while earthly growth symbolizes vile desires and low pleasures arising from the base self in the body's Egypt; tasting them brings humiliation, poverty, and ruin.
rows.anchor: الطعام الواحد هو الغذاء الروحاني من الحكمة والمعرفة وما تنبته الأرض هو الشهوات الخبيثة واللذات الخسيسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mystical cause of this demand is veiling from divine signs, darkening hearts through sin, and heedlessness of the Beloved that replaces the sought goal with other things; the author asks for well-being.
rows.anchor: وسبب طلب ذلك الإحتجاب عن آيات الله تعالى وتجلياته وتسويد القلوب بدرن الذنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fools are either light-minded or people who have degraded their reason through blind imitation and refusal to reflect; the referent broadly includes hypocrites, Jews, and polytheists who reject the qibla change.
rows.anchor: أي الخفاف الأحلام أو المستمهنوها بالتقليد المحض والإعراض عن التدبر والمتبادر منهم ما يشمل سائر المنكرين

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi restricts the fools to the first group, the hypocrites.
rows.anchor: وروى عن السدي الإقتصار على الأول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas restricts the fools to the Jews.
rows.anchor: وعن إبن عباس الإقتصار على الثاني

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan restricts the fools to the polytheists.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن الإقتصار على الثالث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports likely identify groups among those addressed by the revelation rather than restrict its meaning, since the definite plural is general and no reason requires limiting it.
rows.anchor: ولعل المراد بيان طائفة نزلت هذه الآية في حقهم لا حمل الآية عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Announcing the future accusation in advance prepares the listener, softens the shock, prevents confusion, and readies a more decisive answer; its fulfillment after the prediction is a prophetic sign.
rows.anchor: وتقديم الأخبار بالقول على الوقوع لتوطين النفس به فإن مفاجأة المكروه أشد إيلاما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A proposed reason for the advance notice is to teach that the statement stems from foolishness and should not cause distress; the author replies that the exchange itself would teach this even after the event.
rows.anchor: الوجه في التقديم هو التعليم والتنبيه على أن هذا القول أثر السفاهة

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says the verse came after the qibla change and that the future tense means past: enemies had criticized the action and would repeat their criticism.
rows.anchor: وقال القفال : إن الآية نزلت بعد تحويل القبلة

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Al-Baraʾ reports that the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months after arriving in Medina, wished to face the Kaʿba, and then received the revelation beginning قد نرى تقلب وجهك.
rows.anchor: عن البراء رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : لما قدم رسول الله

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: A transmission through Abu Ishaq, ʿUbayd ibn Humayd, and Abu Hatim adds that سيقول السفهاء was revealed as well.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أبي إسحاق وعبيد بن حميد وأبي حاتم عنه زيادة فأنزل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage follows the previous one as criticism of a subsidiary matter after the earlier criticism of fundamentals; the lack of conjunction shows each is independently scandalous.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة الآية لما قبلها أن الأولى قدح في الأصول وهذا في أمر متعلق بالفروع وإنما لم يعطف تنبيها على إستقلال كل منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من الناس is an accusative circumstantial phrase meaning humankind generally; it emphasizes how foolish the accusers are by comparison with the human species.
rows.anchor: في موضع نصب على الحال والمراد منهم الجنس وفائدة ذكره التنبيه على كمال سفاهتهم بالقياس إلى الجنس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading takes الناس to mean unbelievers and clarifies that the accusation came only from the most depraved among the groups, not every individual.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الكفرة وفائدته بيان أن ذلك القول المحكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the generic meaning of people over the restriction to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: والأول أولى كما لا يخفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما ولاهم means “what turned them away”; its root denotes a second thing following the first without interruption, and the question is reproachful.
rows.anchor: أي أي شيء صرفهم وأصله من الولي وهو حصول الثاني بعد الأول من غير فصل والإستفهام للإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their former qibla was Jerusalem; قبلة is derived from facing, originally describing the state of the one faced and conventionally naming the place toward which prayer is directed.
rows.anchor: يعني بيت المقدس وهي فعلة من المقابلة كالوجهة من الواجهة وأصلها الحالة التي كان عليها المقابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing the qibla as one they had followed, after already calling it theirs, intensifies the rebuke; Jews objected because they denied abrogation and disliked Muhammad's divergence from them.
rows.anchor: وفي وصفها بذلك بعد إضافتها إلى ضمير المسلمين تأكيد للإنكار ومدار هذا الإنكار بالنسبة إلى اليهود زعمهم إستحالة النسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews said that Muhammad should return to their qibla so they would follow and believe; the author suspects this was only an attempt to tempt him.
rows.anchor: أرجع إلى قبلتنا نتبعك ونؤمن بك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists sought to attack Islam by claiming that neither facing Jerusalem nor turning away from it had a reason; they said Muhammad abandoned his ancestors' qibla, returned to it, and would return to their religion.
rows.anchor: وبالنسبة إلى مشركي العرب القصد إلى الطعن في الدين وإظهار أن كلا من التوجه إليها والإنصراف عنها بغير داع إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites' objections varied with their backgrounds, since some were Jews and others were not.
rows.anchor: وبالنسبة إلى المنافقين مختلف بإختلاف أصولهم فإن فيهم اليهود وغيرهم

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: A report gives the time facing Jerusalem as sixteen or seventeen months; other reports give nine or ten months from Malik ibn Anas, thirteen from Muʿadh, and seven from al-Sadiq.
rows.anchor: وأختلف الناس في مدة بقائه صلى الله عليه وسلم مستقبلا بيت المقدس ففي رواية البخاري ما علمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There are two views on whether the Prophet faced a different qibla in Mecca; the more famous view says he did not, and this is also narrated from al-Sadiq.
rows.anchor: وهل أستقبل غيره قبل بمكة أم لا قولان أشهرهما الثاني وهو المروي أيضا عن الصادق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All places and directions belong equally to God; no direction is inherently special to Him, and the relevant matter is obedience, since He may command any place or direction for prayer.
rows.anchor: أي جميع الأمكنة والجهات مملوكة له تعالى مستوية بالنسبة إليه عز شأنه لا إختصاص لشيء منها به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is a level road and means what divine wisdom requires: facing Jerusalem at one time and the Kaʿba at another.
rows.anchor: أي طريق مستو وهو ما تقتضيه الحكمة من التوجه إلى بيت المقدس تارة وإلى الكعبة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance clause is an appositional substitute of inclusion from the preceding statement; it explains what justifies the turn toward the Kaʿba, while the earlier clause justifies the former direction.
rows.anchor: والجملة بدل إشتمال مما تقدم وهو إشارة إلى مصحح التولية وهذا إلى مرجحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose the community for this guidance, so they praise Him.
rows.anchor: يخص الله تعالى بها من يشاء ويختار من عباده وقد خصنا بها فله الحمد
